checks: Source 942427a6ff06c7e1 §6 gives the fixed-support rational-chamber claim. The frozen proof makes endpoint and lower-dimensional cells explicit.

Every nonvertical cap can be tightened to the actual mark. For each orientation the clamp is piecewise affine in tilt, with all knots affine in endpoint/mark data and with rational coefficients. Each tail has a finite large-tilt representative and never exceeds the corresponding pure-base cap.

The own interval contributes at least the mark change to the decrease of every fixed-tilt upper cap and to the increase of every lower cap. These two-sided sign bounds survive taking the separate infima.

Lower and upper supporting roof slopes give zero appropriate depth at each own endpoint, with finite slopes at extreme bases. Thus the crossing is unique and interior. On a full-dimensional joint cell the difference has y-slope at most −2, so the rational affine elimination is valid; boundary cells inherit that formula by continuity.

Substitution into the finite joint cell inequalities gives finitely many endpoint chambers. At overlaps uniqueness yields equal values. The finite maximum preserves continuity and rational piecewise affinity. N=0 is half the width.

overlap.comparison: Gives explicit formulas for three positive consecutive intervals after normalization. It does not state the rational chamber structure for arbitrary fixed length.

readability: The joint cells can be taken before imposing convex-roof compatibility, which avoids needing a full-dimensional feasible cell at a roof equality.

summary: The fixed-tilt knot evaluation and unique oriented-minimum crossing yield finite rational affine chambers for the actual optimized raw depth.
